paper.title: An algorithm with nearly optimal pseudo-regret for both stochastic and adversarial bandits

settings.definition_quote: In a stochastic multi-armed bandit problem the rewards for each arm~$i$ are generated by a fixed but unknown probability distribution $\nu_i$ on~$[0,1]$. All rewards $x_i(t)$, $1 \leq i \leq K$, $1 \leq t \leq n$, are generated independently at random with $x_i(t) \sim \nu_i$.
If the selection of rewards $x_i(t)$, $1 \leq i \leq K$, depends on which arms $I_1,\ldots,I_{t-1}$ the player has chosen in the past, then the adversary is called {\em adaptive}.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed adversarial bandit with oblivious adversary

settings.definition_quote: If this is done beforehand (before the player interacts with the environment), then the adversary is called {\em oblivious} as the selection of rewards is independent from the arms~$I_t$ chosen by the player.

source.label: theorem_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $\alpha < 1$, $\epsilon > 0$, $\beta < 2$, and $\clower > 0$. Consider a player that achieves pseudo-regret $\pseudoR_\sto(n) \leq \clower (\log n)^\beta$ for any stochastic bandit problem with two arms and gap~$\Delta=1/8$. Then for large enough $n$ there is an adversarial bandit problem with two arms and an oblivious adversary such that the player suffers regret $R_\obl(n) \geq n^\alpha/8 - 4\sqrt{n \log n}$ with probability at least $1/(16n^{\epsilon}) - 2/n^2$.

results.notes: Regret lower bound holding with small (polynomially decaying) probability, not 1-delta; quantity mapped to high_probability_regret for lack of better term. Algorithm class: players with polylog stochastic pseudo-regret of order beta<2.

source.quote: Furthermore, there is an adversarial bandit problem with two arms and an adaptive adversary such that the player suffers expected regret $\EE{R_\ada(n)} \geq \frac{n^{\alpha-\epsilon}}{128} - 3\sqrt{n \log n}$.

source.quote: For stochastic bandit problems with gaps $\Delta_i$ such that $\Cib\sum_{i:\Delta_i > 0} \frac{\log (n/\delta)}{\Delta_i} \leq \sqrt{nK \log (n/\delta)}$, $T_i(n) \leq C_\sto \frac{\log (n/\delta)}{\Delta_i^2}$ with probability $1-\delta$ for any arm $i$ with $\Delta_i > 0$

results.notes: Bound on number of pulls of each suboptimal arm w.p. 1-delta; constant C_sto unspecified ('suitable constants') so recorded as O.
